lyrics:
Wazoo? He thinks the room is beneath him
Counts every ticket, then insults the seats
Technique, certainly. Feeling? I doubt it
Everything measured; nothing that bleeds
Smarter than everyone. That's the posture
Filth when the difficult music runs long
Calls it satire whenever you catch him
Ask what he loves. He'll tell you what's wrong

So what do we call it
Contempt? Vanity
Cruelty dressed up
as integrity
You made the impression
You fed us the evidence
What else are we meant to believe

I wrote what I heard
I said what I saw
You wanted approval
I wouldn't applaud
Call that contempt
Call honesty ugly
Wazoo in effigy
Guilty

Pretentious, academic — put that in print
Difficult mostly for difficulty's sake
A talent for sneering, a taste for the gutter
He calls it a mirror. I call it a fake
And can he play rock? Well, hardly the question
A loser in costume, impressed with his brain
You'll find this opinion remarkably common
Ask anyone qualified. Ask them again

So what do we call it
Contempt? Vanity
Cruelty dressed up
as integrity
You made the impression
You handed us kindling
What else were we given to hear

I wrote what I heard
I said what I saw
You wanted approval
I wouldn't applaud
Call that contempt
Call honesty ugly
Wazoo in effigy
Guilty

Ask the men who were in the band beside him
Ask what perfection was worth in the end
Three hundred dollars to make both the records
Ten thousand later for hired-in men
A phone call finished what years had assembled
The salaries stopped. As of last week. That's clear
Brilliant, perhaps — but brilliance is cheaper
When somebody else pays the price to be near

So I asked the wild side hero
"Wazoo? The single most untalented person I've heard in my life
Two-bit
Pretentious
Academic
He can't play his way out of anything."
Twenty years later, that same wild man
Stood at a podium and inducted him into the Hall
No correction was printed
Corrections are not printed

By then he was dying. He went there regardless
Germany. Conducting. That unplayable score
They played it. The room stayed on its feet twenty minutes
Sentiment, surely. We've seen it before
No need to revise what was already printed
No reason to soften a judgment because —

Like I invented this

I wrote what I heard

Have I got to listen to this
Talentless

impression.text: This theatrical jazz arrangement immediately establishes a bombastic and cynical emotional atmosphere, driven by a highly dynamic interplay of bright brass, sweeping strings, and a nimble rhythm section. The energy level is intense and dramatic, marked by driving ensemble grooves that frequently give way to abrupt pauses designed to highlight the mocking vocal delivery. Despite the incredibly dense orchestration, the production remains exceptionally clear with a wide soundstage, allowing the crisp, upfront lead vocal to command the mix without being overshadowed by the complex instrumentation. The track is uniquely defined by its sudden structural shifts and narrative interruptions, peaking with a vibrant trumpet solo before abruptly ending on a starkly exposed spoken-word punchline.

review.review_text: Rose has spent 2026 pivoting hard, from the diarist of 'I'm Still Here' to the political sprawl of 'Outlandia,' but nothing in the catalog quite prepares you for this: a full electric orchestra deployed as courtroom, with the critic himself in the dock. The marimba pulse and fragmented brass stabs open in a jittery 7/8 before the whole thing lurches into a 4/4 chorus at a driving clip, and the tension between those meters is the point, an ensemble that keeps snapping shut on itself, abrupt stops leaving the baritone exposed. The genius here is structural: the song reads like a demolition of a man ('Technique, certainly. Feeling? I doubt it') until the third verse quietly turns the knife, 'Three hundred dollars to make both the records; ten thousand later for hired-in men,' and you realize the target may deserve some of this and none of it. Then the bridge lands the real gut-punch, the same wild-side hero who called Wazoo 'the single most untalented person I've heard in my life' standing at a podium twenty years later to induct him, and Rose's flat refrain, 'No correction was printed. Corrections are not printed,' says everything about who actually holds power in the room. The closing trumpet solo tears through the shifting meters before that dry, bored spoken 'Talentless' cuts it dead, an ending that would feel like a stunt if it hadn't been earned. It asks a lot of a listener, and the density means it reveals itself over several passes rather than one, but the craft is unmistakable. A highlight, and one of the most daring things he's put his name to.
